extraction.title_anon: Two young men, 26 and 22, on a motorcycle, Karnataka (death; claims dismissed, vehicle not proved)
extraction.family_summary: In August 2013 two young men, aged 26 and 22, died in a late-night road accident on their motorcycle in Karnataka; their families said a lorry hit them. In April 2015 the tribunal dismissed both families' claims because they had not proved that lorry was involved, and in June 2018 the High Court agreed. In December 2025, more than 12 years after the accident, the Supreme Court dismissed their appeals, so the families received no compensation.
what_mattered: The families could not prove the lorry was involved: the first police complaint named no vehicle, the scene record was made days later, there was no eyewitness, and their witnesses contradicted themselves.
A motor vehicle inspector found no damage at all on the lorry, which the court said did not fit a crash that killed two people; the lorry was traced only about one and a half months later.

Only the balance of probabilities is needed and a missing registration number in the first complaint is not fatal by itself, but the vehicle's link to the accident must still be shown by reliable evidence.
